ca_east_face_17.blurb: The east-facing cliff of Tuolumne Peak sits in the high country north of Tuolumne Meadows, in the May Lake area of Yosemite. It is a trad-only wall, and the grades run from easy fifth class up to about 5.10, with most lines in the 5.7 range, so it suits parties comfortable on moderate alpine rock. The granite looks broken from a distance but is surprisingly sound, with plenty of cracks for gear; bring small cams. The face is a long way from the road and rarely crowded, which makes for a quiet, adventurous day. Water can run down the cliff in snowmelt season. Summit views take in the Meadows and the surrounding peaks.

ca_central_sector.blurb: The Central Sector holds most of the problems at the Bachar Boulders, a bouldering area near June Lake on the Eastern Sierra, at roughly 7,600 feet. The two dozen problems are mainly in the easy to moderate range, from the lowest grades through about V4, with a small number of much harder lines near the top end. Expect finger cracks, seams and pocketed holds. Landings are mostly flat, though a few problems are tall enough that a spotter and extra pads are worth bringing. Many problems are unnamed, and the boulders sit in open forest a short walk from the dirt-road parking.

ca_au_five_and_dime_cliff.blurb: Five and Dime Cliff is a small granite crag in the Lower Merced River Canyon, just below Yosemite Valley, on the north side of the river near Reed's Pinnacle. It holds about two dozen routes, a mix of traditional lines and bolted ones, with a couple of two-pitch climbs. Grades start around 5.7 and reach 5.12, with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.12. Pitches are fairly short, 70 to 130 feet, and a standard Yosemite rack covers the gear lines. The rock quality is excellent and the setting overlooks the river. It works well as an overflow option when nearby crags are busy.

ca_4_goodrich_pinnacle_area.blurb: This section of the Glacier Point Apron, on the south side of Yosemite Valley, covers the slabs left of Monday Morning Slab out to Goodrich Pinnacle, an exfoliation slab on the granite Apron. It is mostly trad, with a few bolted lines, and runs from 5.6 to 5.12, concentrated in the 5.9 to 5.10 range. Many routes are long, from several pitches up to a couple of dozen on the big link-ups. Climbers come for the slabs, which rank among the finest in Yosemite Valley. Rockfall has occurred on the Apron, so judge the terrain above you with care.

ca_echo_cove_east_side.blurb: The east side of Echo Cove is a compact cluster of single-pitch climbs in the central part of Joshua Tree National Park. Most of the roughly two dozen routes are traditional, alongside a handful of top-rope lines and one bolted route. Grades range from 5.6 to 5.12, with the largest group at 5.10. The cove offers a mix of roofs, faces and dihedrals. Some starts are sunny alcoves that stay sheltered on cold, windy days, while other faces sit in shade. Walk-ins are short, which makes it handy for a quick session between other crags.

ca_the_alcove_left.blurb: The Alcove Left is the left-hand side of a bolted sport wall beside a waterfall at Monkeyface Falls, one of the Highway 38 crags in the San Bernardino Mountains, at about 4,700 feet. All two dozen routes are sport climbs, roughly 50 to 80 feet long. A few easy lines and moderate classics around 5.8 to 5.9 exist, but the area is mostly known for steep, sustained climbing in the 5.12 range, with several 5.13 routes. The canyon angle and large trees give plenty of summer shade, so it stays workable even in hot months.
